s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic oral ulcerative lesion with granulomatous inflammation
salient_findings: Ulcer with clean base and heaped-up margins
Intracellular yeasts within histiocytes on histopathological examination
key_facts: 40-year-old man from eastern India
Presented with a nonhealing ulcer on the tongue for 4 months
Lesion started as a small painless mass on the right lateral aspect of the tongue
No history of trauma or tongue bite preceding the lesion
Patient denied consuming tobacco or alcohol regularly
Well-controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus for 2 years with oral hypoglycemic agents
Single well-defined ulcer measuring 2 × 2 cm on the right lateral aspect of tongue
Dense diffuse infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, epithelioid cells, giant cells, plasma cells, eosinophils, and neutrophils on histopathological examination
Intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo within histiocytes
Fungal culture on Sabouraud dextrose agar was negative
HIV-1 and HIV-2 serologic testing were negative

shortlist.label: histoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo within histiocytes, consistent with fungal infection

shortlist.label: tuberculosis of the tongue
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and chronic oral ulcerative lesion, consistent with tuberculosis

shortlist.label: sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and presence of epithelioid cells and giant cells, consistent with sarcoidosis

shortlist.label: cutaneous leishmaniasis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of granulomatous inflammation and histiocytes, consistent with leishmaniasis

shortlist.label: granulomatosis with polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and presence of eosinophils and neutrophils, consistent with granulomatosis with polyangiitis

raw.rationale: The presence of intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo within histiocytes, as seen on histopathological examination, is highly suggestive of histoplasmosis, especially given the patient's geographical location in eastern India, where histoplasmosis is more common.

rejected.label: tuberculosis of the tongue
rejected.why: While tuberculosis can cause ulcers on the tongue, the presence of intracellular yeasts is not typical for tuberculosis.

rejected.label: sarcoidosis
rejected.why: Sarcoidosis typically presents with non-caseating granulomas, which are not described in the histopathological findings.

rejected.label: cutaneous leishmaniasis
rejected.why: Cutaneous leishmaniasis typically presents with skin lesions, and the histopathological findings do not match those of leishmaniasis, which typically shows amastigotes within macrophages.

rejected.label: granulomatosis with polyangiitis
rejected.why: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis is a systemic vasculitis that typically presents with a combination of respiratory, renal, and systemic symptoms, which are not described in the case vignette.
